report:
The argument establishes the exact bounded supplied-fibration result and its stated energy and independence properties. No indispensable step remains unsettled. This verdict concerns the specified special scope; it does not resolve the original general P15.2 problem or certify a priority claim.

The transverse constant argument is valid globally. Proper pushforward of the closed form ω^m is a closed degree-zero current, hence a constant distribution on connected B. Positivity gives a nonnegative constant. Sard applies to the underlying smooth map of real dimensions 2n and 2ν; surjectivity supplies a nonempty regular fibre, whose positive Kähler volume makes the constant strictly positive. Properness makes the critical-value set closed, so fibre integration applies on an open neighbourhood of every regular value. Disconnected regular fibres contribute the sum of their component volumes. The global distributional identity leaves no correction supported on critical values, and requires no volume assignment to exceptional dimension-jumping fibres.

The cohomological assertions follow with the stated hypotheses. θ is smooth semipositive, θ+tκ is Kähler, θ^(ν+1)=0, and θ^νκ^m is strictly positive on the regular locus. Consequently the nef positive-product convention gives numerical dimension ν and volume zero. Stokes proves c_ω V_B=∫X θ^νω^m and representative independence. The de Rham/Bott–Chern parenthesis additionally uses the compact Kähler dd^c lemma, recorded as premise 4. Expanding the finite polynomial gives M_ε=K_ω V_B ε^m+O(ε^(m+1)), with the stated binomial coefficient.

The bounded BT applications have their required antecedents. Local smooth decreasing psh approximations are available by radial convolution on smaller balls; radial means are monotone in the radius. Their holomorphic compositions remain smooth psh, decrease to the specified pullback representatives, and are locally uniformly bounded. This holds on the entire inverse image, including critical points. Properness gives compact support for pulled-back tests, so local BT convergence can be pushed forward. Smooth projection followed by decreasing continuity proves (10). Simultaneous approximation of the horizontal factors proves their vanishing above base degree ν. These arguments do not assume a pullback operation for arbitrary singular currents. Equality in (10) is equality of Borel measures, so (11) legitimately permits the discontinuous weight φ; no discontinuous weight is multiplied into a merely weak limit.

The global mass and test identities also check out. Subtracting the local BT recursion from the smooth-background recursion gives dd^c v∧S=dd^c(vS). The bounded representative defines vS through the measure coefficients of S. Distributional Stokes then replaces factors without changing their total integral. All replacements actually used have positive or semipositive backgrounds, including the extra θ in (18). Testing this identity against a smooth function proves (9). Symmetry, multilinearity and the difference-of-powers identity follow from simultaneous decreasing approximation and linearity; the omitted general nonpluripolar multilinearity proof supplies no missing application.

The decisive perturbation estimate is correct. For each positive mixed product S_j, the smooth forms C_fθ±π*dd^c f are semipositive even at critical points. Their wedges dominate the signed test measure, giving n C_f δ_ε Q_ε. Cohomological replacement yields Q_ε=∫X θ(θ+εω)^(n−1). Its leading exponent is m, and more precisely Q_ε/(K_ω ε^m) tends to (ν/n)V_B. Thus the calibrated perturbation error is O_f(δ_ε), with no ε-relative convergence requirement. For the exact pullback family, the degree-ν term projects to C_φ^ν and every remaining term is positive with total mass O(ε). This proves convergence on smooth tests. Cohomological conservation of mass supplies uniformly bounded calibrated masses, allowing uniform approximation of continuous tests and proving weak convergence with raw mass V_B. No descent of u_ε is used.

The energy proof is valid for all bounded potentials in the claimed backgrounds. Along an affine psh segment, multilinearity makes the energy a finite polynomial. In every integration-by-parts application, the functions are globally bounded differences of globally bounded quasi-psh functions and Θ is a positive closed mixed product of d−1 factors. Premise 1 therefore applies with empty exceptional set. The telescoping differentiation gives e'(t)=∫Y (u−v)T_t^d; integration gives (13), hence the cocycle. Positivity proves monotonicity; conserved mixed masses give the constant-shift law and supremum-norm Lipschitz bound. The second derivative is −d∫Y d(u−v)∧d^c(u−v)∧T_t^(d−1)≤0, proving concavity. The same polynomial calculation supports precisely the claimed differentiable paths in finite-dimensional affine spans, provided they stay in the psh cone.

For the energy limit, the Lipschitz bound eliminates arbitrary perturbative potentials after calibration. The horizontal expansion has no terms of degree greater than ν. The identity Σ_j binom(j,a)binom(n−j,ν−a)=binom(n+1,ν+1) gives exactly the coefficient K_ω E_β(φ). Formula (11), rather than weighted weak convergence, evaluates its bounded Borel weights. Every lower horizontal degree has an extra ε and a cohomologically bounded weighted integral. This proves (2), including discontinuous bounded φ and the stated base variational law.

Auxiliary-class independence is correctly calibrated: the proof works for each Kähler ω with its own positive c_ω, without asserting that c_ω is class independent. For smoothly converging ω_ε with Kähler limit, all finite wedge coefficients converge and c_ωε remains bounded away from zero; the estimates are uniform. The calibration ratio tends to one, establishing both proposed denominators. The compensating change β'=β+dd^c h preserves the currents and the uniform error exactly. Since h is β-psh and h∘π is γ_ε-psh, the relative energy formula applies and gives the reference correction with the asserted minus sign.

The bounded/minimal-type observation uses the admissible zero potential for these nonnegative backgrounds and the global upper bound for quasi-psh functions. It supplies no descent theorem or unbounded extension. Such extensions, degenerate auxiliary limits, nonsmooth manifolds and extraction of a fibration from an arbitrary class are explicitly excluded and are unnecessary for this verdict. Execution records, hashes and compilation supply no mathematical evidence here.

Harmless source typography corrections are that LF657 needs the limiting u rather than the duplicated approximation index, and LF696 needs Θ rather than θ. Neither repairs an indispensable argument: the published bounded integration-by-parts statement is applied directly at its checked hypotheses. The uninvoked exhaustion lemma and weighted-energy proposition do not enter the proof.

passages.statement: On a complex domain of dimension d, locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions v_1,...,v_p, with 1≤p≤d, define a closed positive Bedford–Taylor current dd^c v_1∧...∧dd^c v_p by the recursion dd^c v_1∧T=dd^c(v_1T). It depends only on the currents dd^c v_i. For locally uniformly bounded decreasing psh sequences v_{i,k} converging pointwise to locally bounded psh v_i, the mixed products converge weakly to the product of the limits. Smooth closed factors commute with wedge multiplication and these weak limits. [Bedford–Taylor, Section 2](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf); [BEGZ, Section 1.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2).

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler manifold Y, let Θ be a closed positive current of bidimension (1,1), and let a,b be globally bounded differences of globally bounded quasi-psh functions. Bounded integration by parts gives ∫Y a dd^c b∧Θ=∫Y b dd^c a∧Θ=−∫Y db∧d^c a∧Θ. The measures and integrals are finite, and da∧d^c a∧Θ is a positive measure of finite mass. [BEGZ, Theorem 1.14 with A=∅, Lemma 1.15 and the Dirichlet-measure construction](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2).

For pseudoeffective real (1,1) classes α_1,...,α_p on a compact Kähler manifold Y of dimension d, 1≤p≤d, the positive product is the limit of ⟨(α_1+tκ)...(α_p+tκ)⟩ as t decreases to zero, independent of the perturbing Kähler class κ. For nef classes this product equals the ordinary cup product. With volume defined by the degree-d positive product, a nef class has volume equal to its top self-intersection; for a Kähler representative γ, vol([γ])=∫Y γ^d. [BEGZ, Definition 1.17 and subsequent nef discussion](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2).

If F:M→N is a C∞ map between finite-dimensional smooth manifolds of real dimensions p≥q≥1, its critical-value set F({x:rank dF_x<q}) has measure zero in every coordinate chart of N. [Sard, The measure of the critical values of differentiable maps](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/sard.pdf).
passages.quote: if m>n, the set of critical values of the map (1.1) is of n-dimensional measure zero

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler manifold, every smooth real d-exact (1,1)-form is dd^c h for a smooth real function h. Consequently, smooth real closed (1,1)-forms with the same de Rham class also have the same Bott–Chern class. [Deligne–Griffiths–Morgan–Sullivan, dd^c lemma](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~dennis/publications/PDF/DS-pub-0024.pdf).
passages.quote: then x = dd^c z for some form z.
